architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged melt residence at 120 C, with formulation-dependent thermal-hold drift that is not yet predictably controlled.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min at 120 C, compared with 9.51% for E1 over the same window; each available hold trajectory is only a single run.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Local isothermal evidence consists of only one four-point 120 C trajectory each for E1 and E5 over 15-90 min, with no independent repeats and no hold data for E2 or resin-axis contrasts. Temperature response is supported by multiple six-point 80-130 C sweeps, and realized viscosity uncertainty is at least quantified by E2's three-run spread, whereas repeatability of the hold trajectory is unmeasured.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity during a 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percent without extrapolating beyond the measured window.
Use at least two independent preparations and repeats so the matched-window drift can be compared with the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.

Audit the formulation composition and calculate its reactive mass fraction phi_r before measurement so the frozen H-CORE prediction E1_drift times phi_r and the H-RESIN threshold below one-half of that prediction can be evaluated prospectively.

Use an acrylic-only composition with zero minor tackifier-like fraction if the objective is to discriminate H-DUAL from the claim that acrylic modification alone can produce superlinear drift suppression.

Record preparation and process history and include a fresh-sample viscosity anchor within measured temperature support so drift is not conflated with the large realization-to-realization viscosity displacement already observed for E2.
Preserve realized viscosity level, temperature-response, and thermal-hold results as separate observables; do not infer a molecular reaction pathway from rheology alone.
planner.scientific_question: For an acrylic-only modification of the E2-anchored reactive core, is the matched-window 120 C viscosity drift consistent with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, or is it substantially below that prediction as required by H-RESIN? In particular, can acrylic alone reach the low-drift regime, which would falsify H-DUAL, or does low drift remain absent without the minor tackifier-like axis?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE vs H-DUAL under a near-linear-drift outcome; both predict that acrylic-only S1C49 remains near the linear-dilution prediction, so one acrylic-only experiment cannot positively establish tackifier necessity

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: For S1C49, phi_r = 0.80, so the frozen H-CORE prediction is 9.51% × 0.80 = 7.61% and the H-RESIN acceptance threshold is below 3.80%. A repeat-resolved SI_15_60 below 3.80% supports H-RESIN, falsifies H-CORE by exceeding the 2 percentage-point discrimination margin below its prediction, and falsifies H-DUAL because low drift was achieved with zero minor tackifier.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: An SI_15_60 at or above 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN. A result from 7.61% through approximately 9.61% also agrees with H-CORE within the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. It is consistent with H-DUAL's acrylic-only prediction, but does not establish that a minor tackifier is required because no tackifier-containing contrast is measured.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to 7.61% fails both the stringent H-RESIN support criterion and its at-or-above-linear falsification criterion. Values below about 5.61% would still falsify H-CORE beyond measurement resolution, whereas values from about 5.61% to 7.61% remain compatible with H-CORE within resolution. Additional modifier-axis contrasts would be needed to adjudicate H-DUAL positively.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and at least two independent repeats

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only hold preserves causal isolation and lies at the conservative band boundary, but its external support is explicitly provisional because the literature fraction denominator has not been reverified; 20% has directly commensurate approximately 19-20% anchors.
The 25% acrylic-only hold would test the same hypothesis pairs and is externally supported, but it is a larger perturbation than necessary and lies outside the conservative initial 15-20% test band.

The 20% acrylic plus 5% minor-tackifier hold lies in supported regions and could test mitigation, but activating both axes prevents the requested acrylic-only causal test and cannot falsify H-DUAL by demonstrating low drift without tackifier.

The temperature sweep measures a regression-derived E_eta rather than the failure-mode observable, has lower decision relevance and interpretability, and does not adjudicate the registered thermal-hold drift predictions.
The repeatability experiment addresses process-state displacement but measures viscosity-scale spread rather than SI_15_60, so it cannot directly separate the registered drift mechanisms.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 is an acrylic-only, zero-tackifier intervention at 20% acrylic and phi_r = 0.80. It sits inside the conservative 15-20% acrylic test band and is supported by directly commensurate approximately 19-20% analogue anchors. M-HOLD-120 directly observes the least-resolved and decision-critical isothermal drift coordinate without model fitting or extrapolation. Its predicted 7.61% linear drift and below-3.80% superlinear-suppression threshold are separated by more than the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. The experiment therefore distinguishes H-RESIN from both near-linear alternatives and can falsify the currently relevant tackifier-required claim if acrylic alone reaches low drift, while explicitly not separating H-CORE from H-DUAL when drift remains near linear.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the stand-alone S1C49 hold as the first interpretable experiment with an unmodified E2-core 120 C matched-window hold. This establishes the missing core-matched baseline required by the Skeptic's strongest objection. S1C49 should subsequently be measured concurrently or under the same controlled process block; the single-experiment output schema cannot represent that paired design.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The deterministic rule layer, VOI ranking, tied_top_experiment_ids, and decision-stability sweep were withheld. Therefore S1C49::M-HOLD-120 cannot be established as lying inside the deterministic top set; this false value denotes lack of verification rather than evidence that it ranked below another experiment.
residual_decision_risk: S1C01 alone does not test the acrylic intervention; causal attribution requires a matched S1C49 arm.

robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is design-changing rather than merely interpretive. S1C49 uses the E2 reactive core, while its 7.61% no-effect prediction is scaled from a single E1 hold run despite differences in NCO:OH ratio and core composition. Because E2 has no thermal-hold baseline, S1C49 alone cannot distinguish acrylic-driven suppression from intrinsic E2-core drift. The inventory contains no combined control-plus-treatment experiment card, so the unmodified E2-core M-HOLD-120 experiment should be prioritized and then run alongside S1C49 under matched process conditions. Use at least three independently prepared replicates per composition, prospectively freeze the repeat aggregation and disagreement rule, and verify acrylic reactive-group content before calculating phi_r or thresholds. The direct SI_15_60 observable remains valid, but the current E1-derived causal comparison does not.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, or recommendation_flip_boundary values were supplied, so no weight perturbation that changes the tied top set can be identified or judged scientifically defensible. The proposal's sensitivity to VOI weighting is indeterminate.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The specified 120 C matched-window measurement can directly return SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, so the numerical falsification criterion for H-RESIN is attainable. Practical adjudication is nevertheless under-specified because no repeat aggregation or disagreement rule is frozen, and the 7.61% threshold inherits unquantified uncertainty from a single E1 reference run.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be represented as generally separating H-RESIN from H-DUAL even though a substantial observable interval is non-diagnostic and the numerical criterion for falsifying H-DUAL is borrowed rather than independently registered.
objections.objection: The claimed separation in proposer.hypotheses_separated is outcome-dependent rather than complete. The 7.61% H-CORE prediction and 3.80% H-RESIN support threshold are 3.81 percentage points apart, which exceeds the declared 2.0-point resolution, so that extreme contrast is numerically separable. However, results from 3.80% to 7.61% do not adjudicate H-RESIN versus H-DUAL, and a near-linear result leaves H-CORE and H-DUAL entangled. The narrative admits both limitations, but hypotheses_not_separated lists only the latter. In addition, H-DUAL's registered term 'low-drift regime' has no independent numerical definition; the proposal effectively equates it with the H-RESIN threshold below 3.80%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Support for an acrylic-specific suppression mechanism, rejection of a core-only explanation, and the quantitative use of 7.61% as the correct no-effect expectation would all be unsupported.
objections.objection: The frozen comparator is E1_drift = 9.51%, but S1C49 is built from the E2 reactive core. E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7 and component fractions MDI 0.19287 and polyol 0.80713, whereas E2 has NCO:OH = 1.8 and fractions MDI 0.20191 and polyol 0.79809. No E2 thermal-hold measurement exists and no concurrent unmodified E2 control is included. Therefore the comparison changes reactive-core stoichiometry/composition and adds 20% acrylic at the same time. A deviation from 7.61% cannot uniquely be attributed to acrylic-driven superlinear suppression rather than a different intrinsic E2-core drift. The assumed phi_r = 0.80 also requires the acrylic to be chemically non-reactive; the supplied stoichiometry note explicitly requires recalculation if it contributes reactive groups.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary-observable claim is lost; the limitation lies in the comparator and causal interpretation, not in reading SI_15_60 from the measurement.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C, with no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. The 30- and 45-minute readings provide trajectory checks but are not needed to infer the endpoint ratio.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result near either threshold could be classified differently depending on an unregistered repeat-summary rule, and H-RESIN or H-CORE could be declared falsified despite unresolved reference uncertainty.
objections.objection: An SI_15_60 at or above 7.61% is physically measurable under M-HOLD-120, so H-RESIN's stated falsification event is attainable. However, the protocol only says 'at least two independent repeats' and does not specify whether the decision uses both repeats individually, their mean, a confidence interval, or a repeat-agreement rule. It also treats the 9.51% E1 reference as fixed even though E1 has only one historical hold run, so the declared 2.0-point discrimination resolution does not include uncertainty in the baseline used to calculate 7.61% and 3.80%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be overclaimed as prospectively frozen at the exact candidate level or as identifying the physical cause of suppression rather than only demonstrating a formulation-level drift phenotype.
objections.objection: No target wet-lab result is exposed in the supplied trace, but provenance is incomplete: historical_status states that the current exact v2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. This does not prove outcome leakage, but it prevents independent verification that the exact S1C49 operationalization was frozen prospectively. Separately, M-HOLD-120 can establish superlinear rheological suppression but cannot establish H-RESIN's specific explanation that suppression occurs by lowering encounter frequency of reaction-capable species; no chemical or molecular measurement is planned.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a concurrent M-HOLD-120 control on the unmodified E2 core alongside S1C49, using at least three independently prepared replicates per composition, and define the decision statistic and uncertainty rule prospectively. Verify the acrylic's reactive-group content and recalculate phi_r and stoichiometry before freezing thresholds. To test tackifier necessity positively rather than only potentially falsify it, add a matched 20% acrylic plus 5% minor-tackifier arm and analyze the set as a controlled modifier-axis contrast.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C49 is an E2-core formulation, but its no-effect prediction is scaled from the single-run E1 hold result even though E1 and E2 differ in NCO:OH ratio and core composition and E2 has no hold baseline. Without a concurrent unmodified E2 hold control, intrinsic core behavior is confounded with the acrylic intervention.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
